record.original_question: For every finite set P_n of n points in the plane, does there exist a pair of points p and q in P_n such that every circle containing both p and q contains at least n/4 up to an additive constant c elements of P_n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1 Any set Pn of n points on the plane contains two elements such that any circle containing them contains at least n 4 ± c elements of Pn.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P_n$ be a finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane. For a pair of points $p, q \in P_n$, define $f(p,q)$ to be the minimum, over all circles $C$ in the plane passing through or containing both $p$ and $q$ (i.e., with $p$ and $q$ in the closed disk bounded by $C$), of the number of points of $P_n$ contained in (the closed disk bounded by) $C$. 

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $c$ such that for every finite set $P_n$ of $n$ points in the plane, one can find a pair of points $p, q \in P_n$ with
$$f(p,q) \;\ge\; \frac{n}{4} - c\,?$$
Equivalently, prove or disprove that every $n$-point planar set contains two points such that every circle containing both of them encloses at least $n/4 \pm c$ points of the set.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to Neumann-Lara and Urrutia) that the optimal constant is $n/4$ remains open. Known lower bounds include $\lceil n/3 \rceil$-type results from Hayward, Rappaport, Wenger and subsequent work; a recent 2019 result by Claverol, Huemer et al. improved this to roughly $n(1/2 - 1/\sqrt{12}) + O(1) \approx n/4.7$, still short of the conjectured $n/4$.

status_evidence.title: On circles enclosing many points
status_evidence.snippet: Any set of n points in the plane contains two points such that any circle through them encloses at least n(1/2 - 1/sqrt(12)) + O(1) points.
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower bound is approximately n/4.7, falling short of conjectured n/4.

status_evidence.title: Circles through two points that always enclose many points
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes lower bounds of order n/3 for the number of points enclosed by any circle through a suitable pair.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier bound of roughly n/3 obtained, conjecture n/4 not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Partial Orders and Euclidean Geometry (Urrutia)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the conjecture that any n-point set contains two points such that any circle through them contains at least n/4 ± c points.
status_evidence.claim: Problem stated as an open conjecture.
